column1: # Seed content-discovery wordlist with frequency priors.
# Nmap scans "the most common 1,000 ports" — a list ordered by empirical
# open-ness across the internet. This is the same trick for web paths: the
# prior column orders the request budget toward where content actually lives.
# The priors are ORDINAL SEEDS following practitioner wordlist ordering
# generation's dirsearch/ffuf lists). They are deliberately coarse: the live
# signal is the per-bucket Beta posterior in recon/discovery.py, which is
# recalibrated from our own observed hits run after run. Treat the seed value
# as "where a human pentester would look first", not as a measured frequency.
# prior: 0.0-0.95 seed prior | bucket: path family (drives the learned prior)
# path: leading-slash path; a trailing / marks a directory candidate
